subject: Azure Marketplace: publisher token exchange & offer sanity checks
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@skylineanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Publisher onboarding - token exchange / tenant claim questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for taking this. We're moving our offer into the Azure Marketplace and have hit two blockers during the publisher account setup:

1) The tenant-claim step in the portal requires a token exchange via a service principal. Our DevOps team created an SP but it only has Contributor role for the subscription; the portal expects Owner or a specific delegated role. Can Redwood validate whether Contributor is sufficient for the tenant-claim flow or if we need Owner?

2) The offer manifest check is failing on a field called "publisherId" that our packaging tool inserts. We attached our current manifest (pub_manifest_v1.json) and a screenshot of the claim page (azure-claim-screenshot.png).

Do you have a short checklist you run for this phase (service principal roles, manifest sanity checks, identity proofing) so we can cross-reference? We're targeting a co-sell enablement window the week of June 14, so would like to resolve these by early June.

Attachments: pub_manifest_v1.json (json), azure-claim-screenshot.png (png)

Best,
Asha Reddy
Head of Cloud Partnerships
Skyline Analytics
asha.reddy@skylineanalytics.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@skylineanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Publisher onboarding - token exchange / tenant claim questions

Hi Asha — appreciate the details and the artifacts. Short answers up front, then a suggested checklist and next steps.

TL;DR: Contributor alone is not typically sufficient for tenant-claim in the portal; the portal needs the SP to be able to write the Managed Application / service principal assignments during the claim exchange which requires Owner or a specific role assignment (Marketplace Collaborator / App Owner). We'll validate the exact permission on our side, but plan for Owner for the fastest path.

Checklist (what Redwood will validate):
- Publisher account identity match (company display name / publisherId) — check the manifest publisherId against the portal value.
- Service principal role & tenant consent — confirm SP has Owner or Marketplace-specific role; if you prefer, we can accept a temporary Owner grant scoped to the subscription for the claim operation.
- Offer manifest schema — run a manifest lint (we'll run ours against pub_manifest_v1.json).
- Proof artifacts — gov ID / domain proof if required by the identity gate (we can accept the portal flow or a signed PDF).
- Co-sell readiness flags (if you want co-sell): pricing SKU mapping, marketplace listing assets, and co-sell profile pages.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you assign Owner to the SP for the subscription used for the claim (we can walk through a scoped Az CLI command if useful).
2) I'll run a quick manifest lint on your pub_manifest_v1.json and send a redline before you re-upload.
3) Marissa, can you pick this up for co-sell asset checks once we confirm the identity flow?

We can hold a 30-minute technical validation call tomorrow afternoon (I have 2–3pm PT open). If that works, I'll create a short agenda: token exchange flow, SP permissions, manifest redlines, and the co-sell checklist.

Attachments: tenant_claim_instructions.pdf (we're attaching our standard step-by-step for SP claim flow)

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Publisher onboarding - token exchange / tenant claim questions

Karthik — thanks, that plan is helpful. Quick follow-ups from DevOps:
- They can escalate the SP to Owner for the claim window but want to know whether we should remove Owner immediately after the claim succeeds.
- The pub_manifest_v1.json is attached — two fields they flagged as unknown: publisherId (filled by our packaging tool) and offerPublisherEmail.

Forwarding their note below and attaching the manifest.

We created an SP (redwood-marketplace-sp) and granted Contributor. After the portal rejected the claim we tried Owner but that requires tenant admin consent from our security team. Is it safe to give Owner temporarily while we claim? Also, is there a documented rollback command to remove Owner after claim?

Regards,
Skyline DevOps

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@skylineanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Publisher onboarding - token exchange / tenant claim questions

Thanks for the details, Asha — copying the internal owners so we can move to an operational plan. Naomi: can the identity team confirm that Owner is required versus a narrower Marketplace role (I think we can accept a scoped temporary Owner but want to document rollback steps)? Marissa: once manifest is green, please start co-sell asset onboarding so we can hit the June 14 window. Vivek: will you run the manifest lint and post redlines to MP-4321?

Commitments:
- Naomi will confirm permission granularity by EOD PT tomorrow and provide an Az CLI snippet to remove Owner after claim.
- Vivek will lint pub_manifest_v1.json today and post a short diff.
- Marissa will schedule a 30-minute validation call (I'll propose 2pm PT on 2027-06-01) and own co-sell asset checklist afterwards.

Public notes / guidance for Skyline (summary you can share with security team):
- Temporary Owner grant is an acceptable, commonly-used pattern for the tenant-claim step; we strongly recommend scoping to the minimal subscription and removing the role immediately after the claim completes. Naomi will include the exact rollback commands.
- Confirm publisherId value in your manifest matches the portal publisherId (mismatch is the most common manifest failure).

Action items for Asha/Skyline:
- Assign Owner to redwood-marketplace-sp scoped to the claim subscription for the claim window.
- Share any error screenshots if portal rejects claim after Owner grant.
- Join the technical validation call if possible (we'll keep it focused and technical).

Attachments referenced: pub_manifest_v1.json, tenant_claim_instructions.pdf, azure-claim-screenshot.png

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
